latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1, an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1, and a real t with 0<=t<1. We prove that floor(n t)=m if and only if m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.

By the defining property of the floor function, for any real y and any integer m one has floor(y)=m exactly when m<=y<m+1. Apply this with y=n t. Then
floor(n t)=m  iff  m<=n t<m+1.

Since n>1, in particular n>0. Dividing the displayed inequalities by the positive number n preserves their directions, so
m<=n t<m+1  iff  m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.

Combining the two equivalences gives
floor(n t)=m  iff  m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.
This is exactly the claimed statement.
role_in_parent: Identifies the discrete interval index m associated to a reduced variable t.
statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, and every real t with 0 <= t < 1, one has floor(n*t) = m if and only if m/n <= t < (m+1)/n.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n greater than 1
m is an integer with 0 less than or equal to m and m less than or equal to n minus 1
t is a real with 0 less than or equal to t and t less than 1
floor is applied to the real number n times t
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n greater than 1, for all integers m with 0 <= m <= n minus 1, and for all real t with 0 <= t and t < 1: the statement 'floor of (n times t) equals m' is logically equivalent to the statement 'm divided by n is less than or equal to t and t is strictly less than (m plus 1) divided by n'.
